analysis.title: GS Jee - GS KOREA FINAL RISK OFF 16 Nov 2026
key_insights: KOSPI sold off in a linear fashion after a choppy first hour and is nearing its 5,000 level again. Foreign program outflows accelerated around 10am KST, timed with the index dip, and the desk reads the initial move as passive outflows.
Index turnover was 20% below the recent 20-day average. KRW appreciated 14 bps to W1,335.70.
Semis were the main drag: Samsung Electronics (005930) -4.5% and SK Hynix (000660) -7.9%.

Media reports said a US court found plausible circumstantial evidence of anticompetitive coordination among the big 3 memory makers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron). The cited conduct was simultaneous locking of HBM capacity through LTAs, collective refusal of LTAs for commodity DRAM, and delayed wafer fab capacity expansion.
The desk says the tape felt broadly risk off rather than a reaction to the collusion report, and that sentiment remains feeble.
Foreigners sold $464m of Samsung Electronics, ending a 4-day buying streak, and sold $168m of SK Hynix, which makes 3 straight days of selling.
Defensives outperformed: KOSPI F&B +2.7% (KT&G +2.8%, Samyang Foods +6.2%) and K200 Financials +1.3% (KB FG +1.6%, Hana FG +1.8%).
Local institutions drove the defensive move, buying a net $15m of KOSPI F&B and $18m of KOSPI financials.

market_movers.rationale: Samsung Electronics (005930) fell 4.5% on 16 Nov amid reports of a US court finding plausible circumstantial evidence of memory-maker collusion. Foreigners sold $464m, ending a 4-day buying streak.
SK Hynix (000660) fell 7.9% on 16 Nov, the largest drag on KOSPI. Foreigners sold $168m, a third straight day of selling.
Micron is named with Samsung and SK Hynix in the reported US court finding of plausible anticompetitive coordination on HBM and DRAM long-term agreements.
